### D221. S62: the gas fluctuation field and the spurs — one noise with L1's, the break at the disc's thickness, the shear's stretch, feathers off the chains (BUILD_III Phase L2; a Fable lead on the owner's word, Opus readers and builders)

**Session S62, opened 2026-10-14 on `session-62` from S61's merge.** *How S61 ended:* `verify_clone --ref main` on the tag record 1c05b80 - a fresh clone, the whole suite: **1 439 passed, 5 skipped in 4 h 02 min, specs OK** - the clean full-suite line on the merged state, after the second pass's two record fixes. The owner's word of 2026-10-13: "continue to S62
when S61 closes" and "if S62 finishes, continue with S63 too" — the Fable lead with Opus builders carries on. The
plan's text is `BUILD_III.md` §5 Phase L2 with D219's and D220's added paragraphs; the readings are
`READING_GAS_SPECTRA.md` (23 preprints) and `READING_SPURS.md` (24 sources), both taken during S61's closing suite
by Opus readers under §3e's rules and entered as returned.

**Two stop conditions, resolved in place (§3d: "a source contradicts what this plan assumed"; Fable leads).**
1. *The plan called the gas's height the field's outer scale.* Every source read puts the disc's thickness at the
   spectrum's **break**, not its end: the 2-D column spectrum is a power law from the kpc scales down to the
   thickness and steeper by about one below it (Elmegreen, Kim & Staveley-Smith 2001 §3.3; Block et al. 2010;
   Zhang, Hunter & Elmegreen 2012; Elmegreen & Scalo 2004 §2.1 — a slab thinner than 1/k projects "shallower
   than the 3D density spectrum by one"), and no turnover is seen inside any disc (THINGS to 16 kpc, Dutta et al.
   2013; NGC 5236 and 6946's column-density spectra single power laws to the field, Nandakumar & Dutta 2020,
   2023). **Ruled:** the field has no outer scale of its own — its coarsest scale is L1's ℓ = 190 pc, the one
   noise (D220 II.6), and the cell's unit mean cuts the larger scales as it cuts L1's (#161); **the gas's published
   scale height is the break**, where the octaves' gain steepens.
2. *The break's existence is contested.* With the beam forward-modelled Koch et al. 2020 find single power laws in
   M31, M33 and the Clouds, and Grisdale et al. 2017 find THINGS' breaks at the beam; against them stand the LMC's
   HI (80–100 pc rising to ~150 pc outward, EKS01), the LMC's dust (Block 2010), M33's HI at 110 pc (Combes 2012)
   and the simulations with feedback (Grisdale 2017: 100–200 pc, the HI layer's thickness). **Ruled:** the break
   is built, because the model publishes the height and a field that ignored it would claim the gas is a thin
   sheet at every scale; the sources that see none are recorded beside it, and the slope change is **one**
   (EKS01's and E&S 2004's rule; measured 0.8 in M33's HI to 1.5 in NGC 1058), the factor between the break's
   length and the height **π** (Dutta et al. 2009: 1.5 kpc ↔ z_h 490 ± 90 pc; EKS01's "about the thickness" and
   Combes' simulations' 0.5–3 bracket it).

**Part I — the field, ruled.**

1. *One noise, two maps* (D220 II.6, kept): `gas_fluctuation`'s Gaussian sum is L1's three octaves — the same
   lattice, the same seed path, the same values — **continued finer** on the same path: octaves at 23.75, 11.9 and
   5.9 pc (three more; the finest is the field's resolution and is declared; a shader may stop earlier and say
   so). L1's map (`census_clustering`, σ 1.75, three octaves, its `top` factor) is untouched and its gate test
   stays green; the gas field is its own log-normal map of the six-octave sum with its own width.
2. *The slope.* Above the break the octaves' gain is **L1's s = 1.53** (P(k) ∝ k^−1.53, which the sources'
   −1.6 — THINGS' median, Dutta et al. 2013 Table 2, half the sample within −1.9 to −1.5; the whole sample −0.3 to
   −2.2, mean −1.3, s.d. 0.5 — covers; the Local Group's resolved HI reads −2.2 to −2.7, M33's −2.4, Combes 2012
   Table 3: the range goes in the about). **Below the break the gain is s + 1 = 2.53** for every octave finer than
   π·h(R), h the ring's published gas scale height — a per-ring amplitude ladder on one lattice (rule 5: a point
   function of position, the ring's h and the seed; no stored grid is its definition).
3. *The width.* **σ²_lnΣ = A ln(1 + b² M²), A = 0.11, b = 1/3** (Burkhart & Lazarian 2012 eq. 3 and Table 1,
   solenoidal MHD over M_s 0.4–8.8; their Taurus and IC 5146 fits A = 0.16 and 0.12 with b = 0.5 beside it;
   Federrath et al. 2010's compressive forcing three times wider at M 5.5) at the ring's Mach number — the gas
   velocity dispersion the model publishes over the sound speed of the phase the field stands for (the builder
   reads what the `ism` stage publishes; the clouds' median 6.5 is the molecular census's and is not this). σ_ln
   runs about 0.11 at M 1, 0.28 at M 3, 0.52 at M 10 (derived). The measured galaxy widths — HI 0.19–0.51 dex,
   molecular 0.21–0.64 dex, PHANGS' 0.52–1.18 dex (beam-smoothed, masked, with their gradients) — are a disclosed
   check against the map's width per ring, not a target.
4. *The shear's stretch.* An isotropic field a time t old is read at sheared coordinates (`noise.shear`): strain
   = (dΩ/dlnR)·t with **t = min(1/A, 30 Myr)**, A the ring's Oort constant (Jeffreson & Kruijssen 2018 eq. 23,
   τ = 1/A = 2/[Ω(1 − β)]; M51's interarm clouds live 20–30 Myr and track 1/A inside 70″, Meidt et al. 2015; the
   cap where feedback ends a cloud first: Meidt 2015, PHANGS' 10–30 Myr, Chevance et al. 2020; Koda 2021's
   60–500 Myr beside them). Where t = 1/A the strain is **−2 exactly** (dΩ/dlnR = −2A), so the anisotropy is one
   number for most of the disc and the angle comes out of the shear, not in (the plan's "the disc's own shear and a
   sourced lifetime"; Puerari 2014's trailing interarm filaments and La Vigne's sheared flocculent feathers are
   the check). The shear is applied to **the whole sum**, L1's three octaves included: the clouds' map is L1's
   own evaluation and is not sheared; the gas map is. The two maps therefore differ at the
   coarse scales by the shear alone — declared.
5. *What it multiplies.* The diffuse gas and the diffuse dust the render and the viewer draw per ring (the dust's
   own layer, D206; the gas layer), **not the clouds, the clusters or the HII regions** (the census's). Unit mean
   per level-0 cell by the normaliser on the cell's lattice (`noise.lognormal_normaliser`, S55's instrument), the
   ring's totals exact (rule 2). Layer off: 1.
6. *The reference evaluator and the vectors.* A Python evaluator of the map at any (x, y) and the committed test
   vectors (`layer/vectors.json`, S55's convention) a GLSL twin must match in V7; the per-ring ladder (gains, the
   break's octave index, σ, the strain) published as the field's parameters — synthetic scalars per ring, NaN
   layer off (D215 ruling 5) — and carried on the render's header.
7. *The spurs (feathers).* Built as a composed field on the gas ridge's downstream side, **only off chains**: La
   Vigne, Vogel & Ostriker 2006 see feathers in 45 of 223 spirals, 83 % of those with a well-defined dust lane and
   **none of 52 Scd–Sd** — a flocculent disc (`ngc_4414`'s pin) gets none. Spacing along the arm **10 λ_J,sp**
   with λ_J,sp = c_s² / (G Σ_ridge,peak) (Kim & Ostriker 2006 abstract and §6, the thick-disc value; LVO06's M51
   mean 10.4; KO02's 2.5 and SO06's 5 λ_J,arm in the about; Σ at the ridge's peak from the gas pattern's contrast,
   c_s the model's sound speed — LVO06 assumed 7 km/s). Measured spacings to check against, disclosed: M51 ~200 pc
   inner rising to 500–1000 pc; PAWS' nine gas spurs 276 pc mean; 80–2000 pc over twenty galaxies growing with
   radius (Mandowara 2022 Table 4). Pitch **63° ± 12° from the circle** (Elmegreen 1980, 28 spurs; KO02's
   kinematic wavefront — leading at the ridge, trailing downstream — is the alternative, carried as the look's
   debt); length **240 pc** (Schinnerer 2017's mean; 155–475 pc, Corder 2008); width **60 pc** (the thin parts'
   40–80 pc); the contrast falling along the spur **by ×5–10 from the ridge** (LVO06) — the profile across is a
   declared look (D219's paragraph). The phases — where along each chain the first spur stands — are synthetic,
   on `texture_seed`, per chain. The field multiplies the diffuse gas and dust as the lanes do (the pieces'
   `Stretches` normaliser keeps the ring mean exact). Stellar spurs (Elmegreen 1980's 0.5–10.5 kpc apart, 0.6–4.8
   kpc long) are not built: they are the young stars' light, V5's.
8. *The gate* (judged in place): the evaluator's measured 2-D spectrum on flat patches reads s = 1.53 ± 0.15 above
   π·h and 2.53 ± 0.15 below, with the break within an octave of π·h on three rings; the map's width per ring is
   the relation's at that ring's Mach number (measured on the map); the strain as declared (the anisotropy of the
   map's autocorrelation measured); unit mean per cell to 1e-12 on the lattice; L1's gate test and the clouds'
   map bit-identical; I1–I3; the vectors committed and matched by the evaluator; the spurs' spacing on the Milky
   Way template at R₀ against the disclosed 200–1000 pc; no acceptance row moves; the layer-off run bit-identical.
9. *Order of work.* The reading documents entered; the evaluator and its spectrum probe first (the instrument
   before the thing it certifies: an FFT spectrum tool in `specs/`); the field and its parameters; the render's
   and the viewer's dust and gas layers reading it (a placement reader); the spurs; the reviewer; the re-pins
   (layer-on numbers only: the render's frames, the dusty ratio pin); the frames beside the goals.

**Item 7 amended on the spurs builder's measurement (2026-10-14, before any code; the lead's ruling).** The builder
measured the law on the `milky_way` template from the published fields before building (the S60 lesson): with
c_s = `GAS_DISPERSION` 6 km/s (the model's one sound speed for the ridge's gas; LVO06 assumed 7), Σ_gas 10.92 M☉/pc²
at R_SUN and the gas crest 1.13–1.55 times the ring mean on the five chains there (#155's shortfall; the PHANGS ratio
2.73 against the model's 1.43), Σ_peak is 12.4–16.9 M☉/pc², λ_J,sp 494–678 pc and **10 λ_J,sp = 4.9–6.8 kpc at
R_SUN** (0.69–3.97 kpc at 4 kpc, 6.9–10.3 at 10 kpc); KO02's 2.5 would give 1.2–1.7 kpc, SO06's 5 λ_J 2.5–3.4, Lee
2014's 7.9 3.9–5.4, three arm widths 5.8 kpc. M51's 200–1 000 pc follow from its dust lanes' 100–300 M☉/pc²; a real
Milky Way arm column near 30 would give 2.8 kpc under the same law. **Ruled:** the law stays **10 λ_J,sp** — a
derived spacing is not re-factored for the picture — and the Milky Way's spacing is **a disclosed check recorded
with its inputs**; the choice between Kim & Ostriker 2006's thick-disc 10 and 2002's thin-disc 2.5, both sourced, is
**the owner's** (told below). Expect about one spur per chain crossing at R_SUN and more inside 4 kpc; the mechanism
is built so that it holds when the gas crest is mended. *The graph:* `gas_surface_density` is `sfh_azimuthal`'s, which
requires `star_formation_gas_contrast` from `gas_pattern`, so **`gas_density_contrast` moves to a composing stage
`spurs` after `sfh`**, fed by the layer stage `layer/spurs.py` whose table of spurs (one row a spur: its chain, foot,
spacing, λ_J and Σ_peak) is drawn on `texture_seed`; `star_formation_gas_contrast` stays in `gas_pattern` and
**without spurs, as the lanes are kept out of it** — the young stars' contrast ignores lanes and spurs alike, a
carried note. *The walk* reads the crest contrast on the two grid rings bracketing each foot at the chain's crossing
azimuth, linear between (the point function's first off-grid read solves the mid-gap rings at 1.89 s on the template
and would double the gas pattern's row): a declared approximation, its error against the point function measured on
a sample of feet and tested. *The composition:* g′ = (1 − ⟨S⟩(R))·g + S — the spurs' excess taken from the ring in
proportion to g, the ring mean exact, positive while ⟨S⟩ < 1 (uniform subtraction from the interarm floor would
drive the trough, 1e-44 in places, negative). *The shape:* a straight segment in the log-polar plane (a 63° log-spiral
arc, under a parsec from the plane's straight segment over 240 pc at R_SUN), Gaussian across (FWHM 60 pc), the
amplitude along exp(−ln 7 · t/L) with round caps, the three stretches integrated in closed form with erf as
`Stretches` does; the foot's peak the ridge's crest contrast there.

**Items 2–5 amended on the field builder's measurements (2026-10-14, before the stage was registered; the lead's
ruling).** The instrument came first (`specs/spectrum.py`: a Hann-windowed periodogram normalised to Parseval,
averaged round k in log bins, one law or a continuous broken law by least error; fractals asked for 1.53 and 2.53
read −1.511 and −2.499, a known broken law −1.557 / −2.497 with the break at 0.93 of the truth), then two stops.
(1) *The model publishes no sound speed for the diffuse phase*: `GAS_DISPERSION` 6 km/s is its one dispersion and
the gas pattern's isothermal sound speed too ("there is no second"), so item 3's Mach number would be 1 on every
ring and σ_ln 0.108 — a field standing for nothing; `H2_GAS_DISPERSION` 8 km/s belongs to the pressure
prescription and its about forbids its reuse; the molecular 0.19 km/s is the census's. **Ruled:** the Mach number
is `GAS_DISPERSION` over **the cold neutral medium's isothermal sound speed, one new level-0 constant read before
it enters** (Heiles & Troland 2003's Millennium survey or Wolfire et al. 2003's two-phase equilibrium, fetched and
tagged by the builder; μ 1.27) — the phase between the clouds whose HI column spectra the sources measured; M ≈
8–12 and σ_ln ≈ 0.47–0.55 expected, the measured HI widths (0.19–0.51 dex) the disclosed check. (2) *The literal
mapping of octaves to the break* — an octave below the break when its lattice scale is below π·h — put every octave
below it beyond 5.3 kpc (π·h 228–3 744 pc there, 355 at R_SUN) and the realised breaks at 355–515 pc on every ring,
because value noise is flat up to a quarter cycle per lattice cell and an octave carries the spectrum near four
times its scale. **Ruled:** an octave takes the steep gain when **four times its lattice scale** is below π·h (the
builder's measured alternative: fitted breaks 57 / 157 / 179 / 266 pc against π·h 81 / 121 / 180 / 355 at 1, 3, 5
and 8.2 kpc, slopes −1.43 to −1.72 above and −2.40 to −2.60 below; the break index 4, 4, 3, 3, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, 1, 1,
1 on rings 0–11 and 0 from ring 12, where the whole band lies below the thickness and the field is the steep slope
alone, declared); the gate's rings are 1, R_SUN's and 11, and one outer ring at one slope. (3) Past the gas disc's
last published height (rings 25–31, h NaN) the ladder holds the last finite ring's. (4) The per-cell normaliser at
`cell_quadrature`'s rule would cost ~1 000 s (1.3e9 points × 6 octaves): it is built on L1's lattice (2 points per
47.5 pc), its error against a lattice four times denser measured on three cells and declared as L1's was; the
stage's budget 3 s. (5) The strain per ring as measured: −2 on rings 0–1 only (1/A 14.7 and 27.5 Myr), the 30 Myr cap
binding beyond 1.9 kpc (−1.81 at 2.4 kpc, −1.04 at 8.0, −0.73 at 11.7, −0.23 at 29.5); the anisotropy gate reads
each ring's own strain. The Oort constant is derived from the published circular velocity (none is published).

**The field built (the field builder's second and third passes).** *The constant read:* `CNM_TEMPERATURE` 70 K —
Heiles & Troland 2003's column-weighted median spin temperature of the cold neutral medium at |b| > 10° (ApJ 586,
1067, astro-ph/0207105, §2.1–2.2 and Table 2, fetched and read at S62; 48 K by Gaussian component, 63 K at low
latitude, 77 % of the column below 100 K, the Millennium survey's local Milky Way) — with μ 1.27 gives c_s 0.675 km/s
(Heiles & Troland's own 1.4 m_H, 5 % slower, in the about), **M = 8.90 and σ_ln = 0.501 on every ring** (the
dispersion and the temperature are both constants; the measured HI widths 0.44–1.17 in ln are the disclosed check).
The other constants, each from the readings: six octaves, a slope change of 1.0, the break factor π, the width's A
0.11 and b 1/3, the shear cap 30 Myr. *The stage* at checkpoint 5 publishes `gas_fluctuation_seed`, a new table
`ring` (32 rows: the break octave, the Mach number, σ, the strain, the twist, the normaliser) and the `cell`
column `gas_fluctuation_cell_normaliser`, NaN with the rows kept layer off. *The shear is applied in polar form*
(the lead's confirmation): the field is read at (R, φ − Θ(R)) with dΘ/dlnR the ring's strain — `noise.shear` in each
point's own frame — the twist accumulated ring by ring and published so the read positions stay continuous across
ring edges; L1's map is unsheared. *The cost, measured and accepted:* the normaliser table on L1's lattice (2 points
per 47.5 pc, 5.26 million points, six octaves, float64) 4.6–5.1 s cold — a sparser lattice breaks the declared error
(1.5 points 3e-2, 1 point 7.8e-2 against the 2e-2 limit; 2 points 9.7e-3 rms, 1.83e-2 worst) — **#163**; the lead's
3 s budget was an estimate.

**The spurs built (the spurs builder's second pass; seven commits, cherry-picked).** `layer/spurs.py` is the layer
stage `gas_spurs` (checkpoint 4, `texture_seed`, one stream per chain): it lays the table `gas_spur` — chain, arc

holds the `Spurs` class and the composing stage `spurs` (checkpoint 4), which **now publishes

contrast is 1 and Σ_peak the ring's own column — the law allows it, recorded), `ngc_4414` none; the spacing, a

### D222. BUILD_IV adopted — deployment only: the template bundles, a .NET gateway, two container apps, smoothness measured; the edit panel and the zoomed-in point layer moved into BUILD_III as V9 and V6b; the gateway scaffolded (the owner's rulings of 2026-10-14)

**The owner, in chat, on 2026-10-14**, after a review of the project's structure, the live deployment and the record:
"I want to move away from the staged generation … produce a galaxy right away. If a user wants it they can then
enable edits and change the variables, which should still be grouped for convenience but use whatever makes sense
instead of strictly enforcing a sequential process. The emphasis is now on generating a realistic galaxy and
creating good looking renders from it, including when zoomed in. This also means having some pregenerated galaxies
as templates. The web deployment should have the templates cached so that users can switch between templates and
zoom in or out reasonably smoothly. If they edit the templates it is okay for generation to take a while." Then, on
the gateway: no accounts, but limits and share links, as a project to get modern .NET experience in. Then "please
create a plan to implement this"; then, asked whether the plan could keep to deployment alone, the split; then
**"adopt the plan with your recommendations except for 12, scaffold the project for me."** Written before any code
moved (D113). This entry is written by the Fable session that wrote the plan, beside S62's close on the same branch.

### D223. S63: light by age in the field — `/api/render` returns the starlight young, middle and old, each placed by its own weight; the field mode draws the three (BUILD_III Phase V5; a Fable lead on the owner's word, Opus builders)

**Session S63, opened 2026-10-14 on `session-63` from S62's merge (da1da078ffa7; `verify_clone` of that main running
at the open, its line entered below).** The owner's word: "if S62 finishes, continue with S63 too." The ruling is
BUILD_III §5 Phase V5 as written, with no reading (none is listed) and **no stage changes**: `/api/render` returns
`stars_young`, `stars_middle` and `stars_old` — each the field's light of that age part through the curves on its
own, placed round each ring by its own weight (the young by the gas contrast's law as the censuses read it, the
middle by `sfr_modulation`, the old by the stellar contrast — the three parts and their weights the bright
catalogue's decomposition already holds, D200–D203, S59's point reader) — **summing to `stars` per ring and filter
to rounding**; the field mode draws the three as layers. **The gate:** the closure (the three sum to `stars` to
1e-12 relative per ring and filter, layer on and off); the arm–interarm colour difference measured before and
after with `tools/goal_metrics.py` on the regenerated frames (recorded, not a target); the payload and the timings
rows (`render: whole, rgb` 9.158 s at S62; the route's bytes). Two builders: A the route and its tests, B the viewer
(three layers in the field regime from the route's arrays, the switcher's thumbnails and the picture test);
an Opus reviewer before the merge; the age bounds of the three parts are the catalogue's (the cluster window's
end to 100 Myr, 100 Myr to the middle part's end as `bright.py` declares, the rest old) and are **read from the
code, not chosen**.

**A stop condition before the build, resolved in place (builder A's probe; the lead's ruling).** The plan's "each
through the curves on its own" and "summing to `stars` to rounding" cannot both hold: `spectra.stellar_response`
joins the eight band points with power laws in log–log and adjusts them in twelve multiplicative passes
(`band_consistent`), so the sum of three separately joined spectra — young light blue, old red — is not the joined
total. The anchors close (the three parts' eight band points sum to `disc_sed_*` to 8e-14), the responses do not:
the largest relative miss per ring and filter is **4.9e-6 in rgb, 2.45e-3 in sho and hoo, 2.0e-3 in wfc3, 2.4e-3
in wfc3n** on the default galaxy and the Milky Way (3.98e-6 / 2.27e-3 / 1.79e-3 / 2.25e-3 on `ngc_4414`), the same
departure `_unresolved` states as `closure.response` (pinned near 5e-6 through rgb). **Ruled:** `stars` is unchanged
(the V1/V2 gates stand); **each part is its own spectrum's response scaled per ring and filter by the ring's closure
factor** `stars / Σ parts`, so the three sum to `stars` by construction; the factors are recorded per filter in the
route's header beside `_unresolved`'s, and a test pins them. The alternatives — `stars` redefined as the sum (ΔM_V
−2.3e-6, Δ(B − V) +1.6e-6, the SED pins at 2e-6 re-read), the total split by its own linearisation (a part then its
share of the total's spectrum), or a gate changed to "stated" — are recorded, not taken. **The age bounds are the
code's, not D223's first wording:** young 0 to the cluster window (0.02 Gyr), middle 0.02 to `YOUNG_STAR_AGE`
(0.1 Gyr), old older (`bright.AGE_PARTS`); the young part starts at 0 so the parts cover the field. **The weights as
the code reads them:** the young by `gas_density_contrast` (the clusters sit in the clouds, placed by the gas
pattern; the route ships it as `dust_placement` / `placed_gas`), the middle by `sfr_modulation` normalised per ring
(`bright.part_weights[0]`), the old by `pattern_density_contrast` (what `stars` is placed by); each ring mean 1 to
≤ 1e-13. **The payload:** the parts ship per ring and filter (3 × 4 800 bytes), the middle's weight as one (R, φ)
array (576 000 bytes), the old's `pattern_density_contrast` added as an array, the young pointing to the gas's
placement already shipped — about 1.2 MB over the 7.52 MB, where placed volumes would add 5.2 MB; the viewer
multiplies a part's ring value by its weight at (R, φ). Measured before: `render: whole, rgb` 11.558 s cold on a busy
machine (9.158 at S62), 7 519 776 bytes; the frame's arm over interarm in blue 1.410; the disc-integrated shares,
each part on its own: young 0.1330 B / 0.0851 V, middle 0.0951 / 0.0634, old 0.7719 / 0.8516.

**Built (builder A, the route, four commits; builder B, the viewer, three; both cherry-picked).** *The route:*
`/api/render` returns `stars_young`, `stars_middle`, `stars_old` per ring and filter — `bright.part_anchors`, a
reader of the field's own tables by the same decomposition `resolve` uses (`part_masses` on `AGE_PARTS`: 0–0.02,
0.02–0.1, ≥ 0.1 Gyr), each part's own spectrum's response at the ring's colour temperature times the ring's closure
factor `stars / Σ parts` (1 where a ring has no light) — **summing to `stars` to about 1e-14 per ring and filter on
the three galaxies and every filter set**, placed by their weights keeping each ring's light to 1.6e-15, the same
numbers layer off (rtol 1e-12) with every weight exactly 1, every part non-negative. The factors, pinned per filter
at 1e-3 relative: rgb 4.9015e-6 / 2.904e-6 / 1.5652e-6, sho 9.534e-4 / 1.2172e-3 / 2.4408e-3, hoo 1.2172e-3 /
2.4408e-3 / 2.4408e-3, wfc3 5.469e-5 / 2.0088e-3 / 8.444e-4, wfc3n 8.934e-4 / 1.2194e-3 / 2.4162e-3 (default and
Milky Way identical; `ngc_4414` 3.9761e-6 … 2.2633e-3). The shares of the disc's light, pinned at 2e-6 (default,

**Session S64, opened 2026-10-15 on `session-64` from S63's merge (`main` 01c4d4e; S63's `verify_clone` of main had read
3 failed — two timing flakes green alone and `test_audit`'s register pin one session stale, fixed at 01c4d4e — so the

orchestrating the project. fable usage is limited, so spawn opus subagents to do work that doesn't benefit much from

**The six stop conditions and their rulings.** (1) *The clouds' extinction law contradicts the rings'.* The census's
`central_extinction_v` is 2.9696 mag for every cloud — solar dust per hydrogen, one surface density (Σ_GMC 42 M☉/pc²),
no metallicity — while the rings' A_V per unit gas is the dust-to-gas ratio times the grain cross-section: 6.3× the
cloud law at R = 2 kpc, 0.15× at R = 14 (Milky Way). A cloud drawn at its published A_V would not carry the extinction
it takes from the ring. **Ruled:** `/api/clouds` gains an API-derived column `cloud_dust_extinction_v`, the cloud's
face-on mean A_V from its own dust — `cloud_mass` × `dust_to_gas_ratio` × (`dust_extinction_v` / `dust_surface_density`)
at the ring of `cloud_birth_radius`, over π `cloud_size`² (the radius) — every term a published field, no constant on the
wire, no stage change (D4; the pattern of `/api/clusters`' `response`). Since every cloud's mass over its area is the one
surface density, the column depends on the birth radius alone: median 1.897 mag (p90 12.64, max 26.23) on the Milky Way,
4.606 on `ngc_4414`. The stage's own law stays for the region regime's interiors; the two disagree — **#167**. (2) *The
clouds' layer is not the dust's.* `cloud_layer_height` (178 pc Milky Way, 477 pc `ngc_4414`; half the thin disc, a guess,
#95) is up to 3.8× / 5.6× the gas layer the diffuse dust sits in and D211's heating and the scattering were computed for,
and the clouds hold 0.49–0.63 of the disc's dust. **Ruled:** each cloud sits at its own published `cloud_height` (the
plan's "at the clouds' height"), `dust_scattered` and `dust_thermal` unchanged — **#168**: half the dust now sits in a
geometry the energy balance was not computed in; the mend is #95's closure with D211's geometry re-done. (3) *"The
smooth Hα layer reduced by what the points carry" goes negative.* The knots' Hα sums to 0.921 of the field's HII Hα
(Milky Way; 1.081 `ngc_4414`) and exceeds it in 10 of 26 lit rings and 22 % of level-0 cells (29 % of the light); a
remainder clipped at zero loses 4.7 % per ring (Milky Way), 25.5 % (`ngc_4414`), 32 % per cell. The per-ring ratios
0.53–1.43 are the census's own heavy-tailed draw (√⟨L²⟩/⟨L⟩ 6.8 over ~500 knots a ring gives ±0.30), not a defect.
**Ruled:** per level-0 cell c, the field's HII layers are scaled by 1 − D_c / K_c, D_c the Hα of the knots a viewer
draws in c, K_c the Hα of every knot named by c — a share in [0, 1], never negative, no clip — and, amended on the
builder's finding (a cell that names no knot kept its whole field, 1.29 % of the Milky Way's HII Hα, 5.5 % of
`ngc_4414`'s), a knotless cell takes 1 − d, d the drawn share of the whole census's Hα: with every knot drawn the screen
carries the census exactly, with none the field, between them the undrawn fraction of the field. (4) *"Bright stars by
tiles to 10⁶" at whole-galaxy scale.* 10⁶ stars over the disc need l_min 2 251 L☉; the whole disc at that depth is 310 s
cold and 92.7 MB (105.6 with the rgb response); the route refuses past 200 000; and today's request (`n` + `view=`) is
view-keyed, which the owner's sentence forbids for any answer V6 adds. **Ruled:** the tile form (`cells=` level-0 ids +
`l_min` on the 0.05 dex grid, each answer the same bytes twice), the cap per request, an expected-count table per tile
per threshold so the viewer picks ONE threshold a frame against a point budget, a remainder-only render request (the
remainder is exactly two per-ring arrays times placing weights already on the wire: residual 3.5e-15; 9.6 kB against
10.4 MB), the `view=` request retired from the viewer; the 10⁶ is the tiles' depth, never a count drawn at once. (5)
*"Sized by its bubble when resolved."* The bubble exceeds the Strömgren sphere in 99.7 % of knots; by the bubble 51 % of
the Hα would be resolved at the frame's 39 pc pixel, by R_S 4.9 %. **Ruled:** the knot is sized by its Strömgren
radius, where its line light is; the shell is V3's own object; the plan's word is superseded by what the model
publishes. (6) *T6 at galaxy scale draws nothing:* the median cluster's 2 r_h (0.445 pc) fills a pixel only below a
0.91 kpc view width, the largest below 6.1 kpc. **Ruled:** the Plummer profile (a = r_h / 1.305, the plan's) replaces a
cluster's point where 2 r_h ≥ one pixel in the star-first mode (the region regime's clusters keep their sprite, #170); a
20 kpc frame is byte-identical with it on and off.

**Built, round 1 (Opus builder 1, the clouds; builder 3a, the depth composite; in worktrees cut from `session-64`,
cherry-picked).** *The clouds (R1–R4):* `/api/clouds` carries `cloud_dust_extinction_v` and `precision=f4` (2 689 008 →
1 629 600 bytes); `/api/render` carries `dust_diffuse_share` per ring — 1 less the ring's REALISED clouds' dust over its
published dust, summed off the ring-first draw's own mass and radius streams (27.6 ms, no census materialised, the same

× dust_diffuse_share(R)", the two layers, the closure and the expected share (the ring's molecular fraction, 0.827 at

give the τ-weighted mean entry; NaN or zero A_V writes `NO_FRONT` (B9); the GLSL and its TS twin pinned (S55's text

### D226. S66: the layer in the viewer — the noise's GLSL twin held to the vectors, the diffuse dust and the young starlight modulated per sub-step in the march, the spurs drawn from their table, the bar's body and lanes read as the grid resolves them (BUILD_III Phase V7; a Fable lead on the owner's standing order, an Opus probe, two Opus builders and an Opus reviewer)

**Session S66, opened 2026-10-16 on `session-66` from S65's merge (`main` 3794fc3, the tag record; S65's
`verify_clone` of main running detached through this session, its line below), a fresh Fable lead on the owner's
standing order to run the sessions back to back, Opus for the probe, the builders, the reviewer and the close's
documents; usage at the open 5-hour 16 %, weekly all-models 40 %, Fable 51 %.** The phase's text (BUILD_III V7: the
GLSL twin of the noise matching the vectors to 1e-5; the diffuse dust modulated per pixel in the march; the spurs;
the bar's body and lanes; the "physics only" switch; the young starlight of V5 modulated per pixel by the clustering
field, its finest scales dropped with age as L1 rules for the bright catalogue, unit mean per cell keeping each
ring's light; the gate the vectors, the frame-time readout, each ring's dust on screen unchanged by the layer) was
probed before the build, as S63–S65 were. **The probe's measurements (its scripts in the lead's scratchpad,
`probe_s66/`):** a float32 twin of every noise primitive (the hash in Math.imul, the floats in Math.fround) is
bit-exact to `vectors.json`'s float32 column on all 528 vectors of the five noise sections and within 5.5e-7 of
float64; the `gas_fluctuation` section's 56 sums are 2.5e-3 off float64 and 2.9e-3 off numpy's own float32, and
**the whole gap is the polar read's transcendentals** — given numpy's float32 read positions the twin's sum is
numpy's to the bit; a float32 position at 26 kpc has an ulp of 1.9e-6 kpc, 4e-4 on g by itself, and GLSL ES 3.00
states no precision for sin, cos or atan; three r186 compiles every ShaderMaterial as `#version 300 es` with
`precision highp int`, so the 32-bit hash is available in the march today. The render grid is 400 × 360 (75 pc by
1°): against the model's point function on a 10 pc mesh the bar's lanes (FWHM 0.1 a = 521 pc) and body
(`pattern_density_contrast`, 0.83–1.35 at 0.5 a) read bilinearly from the cell texture within 0.5 % rms / 0.8 %
max, while the spurs (FWHM 60 pc, length 240 pc; 48 rows on the Milky Way, none on `ngc_4414`) lose 16–47 % of
their crest to the texel (48–66 % max). The gas map's unit mean holds on L1's lattice; on the 1024-frame's 39 pc
pixels the dust's linear column per **level-0** ring is off by 1.2e-2 at worst (rms 3.5e-3; `ngc_4414` 6.3e-3), the
whole dust-only frame by ≤ 1.7e-3, the render's 75 pc rings by up to 0.16–0.30 (too few pixels); the **transmitted**
light rises by Jensen's gap, +2.4 % at R_SUN face-on on the Milky Way, +24 % on ring 1, +8.5 % at R_SUN inclined 60°
— a clumped medium of the same column is more transparent. Along 1 000 inclined rays through the dust's layer ln m
varies by rms 0.45–0.49, the field's whole σ (0.50): read once per pixel the column is off by 45–81 % rms. The young
part is 0–20 Myr and keeps every clustering octave (L1 drops the 47.5 pc octave past 23.87 Myr, the 95 pc past
31.18, the 190 pc past 40.71); of the middle part's 20–100 Myr light 2.9 % (bolometric; 3.4 % in V) keeps three
octaves, 4.4 % (5.8 %) two, 4.3 % (6.6 %) one; the truncated maps plateau (cell-mean medians 0.283 and 0.409 for
one and two octaves, #162) so each must be divided by its own cell mean, published for the full map only; the
mixture's per-ring sampling on 39 pc pixels 4.1e-2 worst (rms 1.2e-2). The cost at the cap (96 steps, 8 sub-steps,
262 144 px) ≤ 143 G integer-and-float ops a frame, estimated 5–10 ms on the owner's RTX 4070. `/api/render`'s
header carried nothing of either field (D221 item 6 had said it would; `/api/arrays` served the gas columns,
`/api/clouds` the clustering header); the picture test printed each capture's ready time and kept it nowhere.

**Ruled (the lead, on the measurement; `RULING_S66.md`, R1–R10; the mechanism the plan's, the tolerances what
they can honestly be, the owner told).** (R1) **The 1e-5 is the noise's:** every primitive section bit-exact to the
float32 column and within 1e-6 of float64, in vitest and in the GLSL itself on the GPU; the vectors' `gas_fluctuation`
section **gains the float32 read positions** numpy evaluated each sum at (a regeneration of that section alone, the
noise sections byte for byte — this decision's act) and the sum given them is held to 1e-5; the read positions
themselves carry float32's geometry, declared: g within 5e-3 of float64, the map within 1e-3 relative — in words,
the shader draws the field at positions within ~0.03 pc of the reference's, a thirtieth of the finest octave's
5.9 pc. (R2) **"Each ring's dust on screen unchanged" is the dust's column per level-0 ring, a sampling tolerance:**
the dust-only frame's `__galaxygenFrameSum` with the modulation on over off within 3e-3; per level-0 ring on the
frame's pixel lattice the column with the map over without within 1.5e-2 (both templates), from the reference
evaluator; the transmitted light is not held — its rise is the mechanism's physics, recorded, and the
layered-over-physics pin moves and is re-pinned once with its direction predicted here (the layered frame transmits
more light, the ratio falls). (R3) **"Per pixel" — first ruled per sub-step** at the sub-step's read point, on the drift the probe measured
along inclined rays, **and amended after the first capture to one read per ray at its midplane crossing** (the maps
are face-on column maps read as a thin screen; the per-sub-step read drew every feature as a pillar through the
layer — the paragraph on round 2 below has the picture and the reasoning), the value multiplying the dust's
placement where it stands for the dust's own column (the depth, the thermal light, the diagnostic) and not the

### D228. S67: the region regime's clouds stop drawing as black holes — the field dimmed only behind them (#112's field half, discharged with #112), and each cloud at its own column (#167's region half) (BUILD_III Phase V8, a side session of S67's lead; Opus)

**What the owner saw (2026-10-18).** Zoomed into the field mode, the "clouds as extinction" were near-solid black
spheres. The lead's diagnosis, confirmed: (1) the region regime's transmission pass multiplied the field's whole
light along a ray by the clouds' T — the light in front of a cloud as well (RULING_S64 R9's stated approximation,
#112's field half), so a cloud at the midplane, which hides about half the layer's light, took all of it; (2) every
cloud took the census's one central A_V, `cloud_extinction_v` = 2.97 mag (#167), as a hard-edged uniform sphere.
Nothing in the model changed.

**R1, the field's light by depth (#112's field half; VIEWER_TASKS T5's recorded mend).** The march gains a third
pass (mode 2) whose image multiplies the field: the field's light along each ray is placed where the stars' layer
puts it — sech²(y / 2h) / 4h at the render header's `layers.stars` (0.356 kpc on the Milky Way), FieldVolume's own
profile, so the share in front of a height is a difference of tanh over the ray's whole span to the layer's far face
(`region.ts layerDepthShare`) — and cut into K slabs of equal light; every cloud sample's optical depth dims the
slabs whose middles lie beyond it, and the factor is the slabs' mean transmission. The march sums the slabs as it
passes the samples (`marchFieldTransmission`, held to the order-free definition `fieldTransmissionBySlabs` on
depth-ordered rays to 1e-12), so no slab is stored and K costs nothing. With no cloud on a ray the factor is K / K,
exactly 1. The star points keep mode 1's target (the whole ray's T and the clouds' front, S64), which no longer
multiplies the frame. **K = 1024, from a measured convergence (A9)**: on the Milky Way's zoom stand in the field mode
(e2e/captures.json milky_way-zoom; 128 × 128 rays through the region's table, its 44 clouds), the worst ray's
summed light moves from K / 2 to K by 0.0114 at 64, 0.0058 at 128, 0.0027 at 256, 0.0013 at 512, **0.0009 at 1024**,
0.0004 at 2048 — about 1 / K, an opaque cloud's edge crossing a slab's middle — while the frame's mean factor moves
by under 1e-4 from K = 8 (`regionSlabs.test.ts` FIELD_SLABS_MEASURED, re-measured against a live API when asked).
**Stated, not mended:** (i) the field's light is placed by the stars' layer alone — the ionized gas's thicker layers
and the field's own diffuse dust between the slabs are not split by depth; (ii) where two clouds overlap on a ray a
sample can arrive behind one already passed (the near-surface sort), and it then dims from the slabs already
reached — the march's stated approximation for overlaps (#112's text), now the field's too; (iii) a ray running
level through the layer, or a ray leaving it away from it, takes the whole ray's T, as before.

**R2, each cloud at its own column (#167's region half).** `packObjects` reads each cloud's `/api/clouds`
`cloud_dust_extinction_v` — the face-on mean A_V over its disc π `cloud_size`², the column D224 publishes and the
galaxy-scale raster already draws — as a uniform sphere of that mean column: κ = (3/4) τ̄ / r (the chord's mean over
the projected disc is (4/3) κ r), so the centre's column is 1.5 τ̄ (`kappaOfMeanColumn`). A cloud without the column
is not drawn (B9). The interior noise (`cloudInterior`) is unchanged. The census scalar `cloud_extinction_v` is now
read by no drawing; the stage's law and the column still disagree (#167 carried: its mend is the stage's).

**The gates.** A synthetic cloud at the midplane, face-on, at 1000 mag dims a uniform field to the light in front of
its first sample, 0.469 — about half — where the whole ray's T gave 0 (`regionSlabs.test.ts`); a cloud of the

### D229. S67: the clouds' layer from a read source — `MOLECULAR_LAYER_FWHM` 120 pc, the clouds' sech² scale height 34.04 pc at every radius and for every template (#95's height part discharged, #180 opened) (BUILD_III Phase V8, S67; the lead's ruling, an Opus builder)

**The owner's words (2026-10-18).** "Read a source for the clouds' scale height and fix the layer in the model before I
retune." D228 had measured the cause of the whole-galaxy clouds' near-black blobs: the clouds' published heights, a
sech² layer at `CLOUD_LAYER_SHARE` 0.5 of the thin disc's scale height (177.8 pc Milky Way, 477 pc `ngc_4414`; "a stated
guess with no source", #95), realised |z| to 1.95 kpc.

**The reading** (a blind Opus reader, 2026-10-18; `docs/READING_CLOUD_LAYER.md`). The Milky Way's molecular layer at
R0 is FWHM 120 ± 18 pc, roughly independent of R from 2 kpc to R0 (Bronfman et al. 1988 via Ferrière 2001 §II.A), 118 pc
(Bronfman et al. 2000 §4.1, read), 136 ± 17 pc (Clemens, Sanders & Scoville 1988 via Ferrière), Malhotra 1994's σ_z
58 pc at R0 (FWHM 137); massive clouds as thin as the CO layer or thinner (Stark & Lee 2005: ~35 pc below 2 × 10⁵ M☉);
the layer flares outside R0 (Nakanishi & Sofue 2006, 160-186 pc at 8-11 kpc) and the sources conflict inside it
(Marasco et al. 2017 falling, Malhotra and Nakanishi & Sofue rising); edge-on spirals' CO σ = 31-89 pc + 1-5 pc/kpc × R
(Yim et al. 2014). Heyer & Dame 2015 was not read (403).

**The ruling (the lead's).**
1. *An absolute thickness, not a share of the stellar disc* (a share would mix the sech² and exponential shapes'
   FWHM): the level-0 `Constant` `MOLECULAR_LAYER_FWHM` = 120 pc, `[verified: Bronfman et al. 1988 via Ferrière 2001 §II.A]` with the two
   neighbours in its about, in the clouds stage's `reads_constants`. The cloud layer's sech²(z/2h) scale height is
   the h whose FWHM that is: sech²(x) = 1/2 at x = artanh(1/√2), so FWHM = 4 artanh(1/√2) h = 3.5255 h and
   h = 120 / 3.5254943 = **34.0378 pc**, derived in code (`clouds.SECH2_FWHM_PER_SCALE_HEIGHT`,
   `clouds.cloud_layer_height(constants)`), with a test by hand (the profile's half maximum at ±FWHM/2,
   `test_the_cloud_layer_s_half_maximum_is_at_half_the_measured_fwhm`). `CLOUD_LAYER_SHARE` and
   `cloud_layer_height(h_thin)` are retired: the function keeps its name and takes the model's constants; the
   clouds stage no longer requires `thin_disc_scale_height`.
2. *One value at every radius and for every template*: `ngc_4414` takes the Milky Way's measured layer, disclosed
   against Yim et al. 2014's edge-on CO widths, which bracket it. The flaring, the conflict inside R0 and the mass
   dependence are **#180**, not built.
3. *The draw is unchanged*: the same ring-first uniforms (`systems_seed, "cloud", ring, "height"`), z = 2h·artanh(2u−1),
   the clip at ±0.999999 kept (14.5 h = 494 pc); every cloud keeps its sign and rank and moves by h_new / h_old -
   0.1914 on the Milky Way, 0.07133 on `ngc_4414`. Cluster heights follow by copy.
4. *The HII and lines layers keep reading the cloud layer* (`/api/render`'s `layers.halpha_hii` = `lines_hii`, and the
   `clouds` entry's `clouds_scale_height`), now the new h from the model's constants, not the thin disc's height,
   which left the two components' `fields`. Bronfman et al. 2000's OB layer (FWHM 73 pc, 0.62 of the molecular) is a
   disclosed check, not a pin.

**Measured.** The census's |z| (the whole disc, `/api/clouds`), before → after: the Milky Way (16 577 clouds) median
196.7 → 37.64 pc, p90 523.7 → 100.2 pc, max 1953.5 → 373.9 pc (D228's probe read 196.7 / 523.7 / 1953.5 before); `ngc_4414`
(6 530) median 530.0 → 37.81 pc, p90 1385.5 → 98.82 pc, max 5980.5 → 426.6 pc (the before by the exact ratio, the draw
being the same uniforms). Over the rings holding more than 1 % of the peak molecular surface density the clouds' h over
the gas layer's is now 0.34-1.60 (Milky Way) and 0.24-1.22 (`ngc_4414`), where it was 1.76-8.35 and 3.42-17.1 (#168's
"3.8× / 5.6×" were S64's, their definition not recorded, and are stale). **On screen**, D228's harness (the session's
notes, `s67-clouds-galaxy-probe`: the frame's linear pixels read before tone mapping by an uncommitted probe, applied
and taken back), the Milky Way's field capture at the template camera and its display defaults, "clouds as extinction"
on over off (switched on for the measurement only; the defaults keep it off), over the 248 428 disc pixels brighter
than 40/255: the darkest pixel keeps **0.053** (D228: 0.033), the 0.1 % quantile **0.320** (0.135), the 1 % quantile
**0.442** (0.288); 1.8 % of the disc pixels lose more than half (2.9 %), 10.9 % more than 5 %; in display 0.231 / 0.458 /
0.601 (0.131 / 0.249 / 0.454); the frame's linear sum on / off 0.957. The clouds now sit in the stars' midplane, where
half the stars' light is in front of them, not 0.6-1.2 kpc above most of it.

**Specs unchanged**: `uv run python -m galaxy.specs` reads the same, line for line, before and after but for the
timings - both models 12 pass / 20 fail / 5 not-yet-computable of 37, `ngc_4414`'s template checks 0 / 5 / 0.

**Re-pins, each with its reason.** `tests/test_clouds.py` (positions and abundances): the median |z| from the new h
(was 0.5 × `thin_disc_scale_height`), and the new by-hand test of the half maximum. `tests/test_render.py` (the
nebular split): `layers["halpha_hii"]` = 0.120 / 3.5254943 kpc (was 0.5 × the thin disc's height / 1000), and the
HII component's fields `["halpha_surface_brightness_hii", "gas_density_contrast"]` (was with `thin_disc_scale_height`
last). `tests/layer_reference.py`: a by-decision carve-out in `normalise` (`_s67_cloud_layer`, naming D229) puts S55's

(exact, a power of two) and `thin_disc_scale_height` back at the end of the two HII components' fields - so every other

### D230. S67: the galaxy-scale clouds flattened to their layer and stretched along the gas field's shear (BUILD_III Phase V8, S67; the lead's ruling and the owner's choice, an Opus side session)

**The owner's words (2026-10-18).** "even a very low cloud extinction turns the milky way galaxy into many black orbs in
the center, this doesn't seem right?", then "i thought cloud extinction is like a lane of dust, why is ours globe shaped
orbs that seem to overlap with stars". Of the measured options (the session's notes, s67-orbs-findings and -2) the owner
chose "Flatten big clouds (viewer)", "Smaller giant clouds (model)" and "Stretch clouds along arms" - not the young
light's thin layer and not the resolved-only raster on its own. The model's size law is the lead's, built separately.

**What was measured first (the template camera, field mode, the owner's defaults, linear light, clouds on over off).**
The orbs are single giant clouds, 150-270 pc in radius (Σ fixed at 42 Msun/pc², r = sqrt(M / pi Σ)), drawn as uniform
discs, opaque at any useful strength: their A_V is 5-25 mag inside 5 kpc under every dust-to-gas law tried. They
go below the ~0.45 a midplane cloud should leave because the raster's slab took each cloud's radius as its
vertical half-thickness (110-260 pc against a 34 pc layer, D229), and the dust's own light at the owner's x4 lies
inside it. The clouds follow the arms as the lane's dust does (A_V x area-weighted placement 2.08, the lane's own 1 +
rms² = 2.08) - their shape, not their place, made the orbs. The sampled stars are undimmed by any field dust (they draw
on 0.1 % of disc pixels at this camera); what shows through an orb is the front of the stellar layer.

**R1, the lead's ruling (an amendment of D224's R3).** Each cloud's vertical half-extent in the galaxy-scale raster's
slab is capped at the clouds' published layer's half-maximum: the render header's `clouds.layers.clouds_scale_height` h
(34.04 pc), HWHM = 2 ln(1 + sqrt 2) h = 1.7627 h = 60.0 pc (`SECH2_HWHM_PER_H`). Applied to each cloud's radius term in
the slab (cloudOpacity.ts `cloudRaster`, `verticalCap`), not to the slab as a whole: the A_V-weighted spread of
distinct clouds' published heights within a texel stays, since it is where their dust is; a texel holding one cloud is
that cloud at its height, at most 60 pc thick each way. The face-on raster is unchanged to the bit (tested), every
height untouched; the march, its twin `composeStep` and the points' `dustTo` all read the slab as built, so none of them
changed and the twin's tests hold as they were. A variance-matched uniform slab (half-width sqrt 3 x the sech²'s rms,
3.14 h = 107 pc) was the other well-defined bound; the half-maximum is the ruling's and the tighter.

**R2, the owner's choice: each cloud an ellipse along the gas field's shear - a read source for the direction and the
default ratio, a tuning control for its strength.** The gas fluctuation field (D221) is read at each point rotated by
theta(R) = sense (twist + strain ln(R / R_r)); the Jacobian of that read is, in the local (radial, azimuthal) frame, the
simple shear [[1, 0], [-k, 1]] with k = sense x strain, so a round feature of the field is, in the disc, an ellipse of
shape [[1, k], [k, 1 + k²]]: axis ratio lambda+ = 1 + k²/2 + |k| sqrt(1 + k²/4), long axis along (k, lambda+ - 1)
(`shearEllipse`, tested against the read's own finite-difference Jacobian). On the Milky Way the published strain gives
lambda+ 5.83 inside 2 kpc, 3.95 at 4 kpc, 2.72 at R0 and 1.3 at 30 kpc. Each cloud is deposited as an ellipse of its own
area pi r² (semi-axes r sqrt q and r / sqrt q, the same uniform-spheroid chord profile), q = lambda+ ^ e, e the tuning
control **"cloud elongation"** (group March, 0-2, default **1**: the field's own shear, so the default's shape is the
read source's; 0 round). A_V x area is conserved per cloud (tested to 1e-6), the ellipse's direction and axes' ratio
are held by the deposit's second moments (the angle to 0.02 rad, the ratio to 5 % on 5 pc texels). With the randomness layer off the field's seed is null:
no shear, every cloud round (the physics-only frame unchanged). A display choice in its exponent; recorded as such.

**Measured, before and after (the same camera; linear light, clouds on over off).**

| | darkest | 0.1 % | 1 % | dimmed > 5 % | < 0.45 | 60 largest orbs: darkest (median) / mean (median) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 0.053 | 0.320 | 0.442 | 10.9 % | 1.10 % | 0.339 / 0.553 |
| R1 alone (elongation 0) | 0.070 | 0.364 | 0.510 | 10.2 % | 0.46 % | 0.412 / 0.626 |
| R1 + R2 (the default) | 0.075 | 0.368 | 0.511 | 10.9 % | 0.43 % | 0.388 / 0.622 |

In display (tone-mapped) the 1 % quantile goes 0.601 -> 0.657 and the darkest 0.230 -> 0.242. The clouds read as streaks
along the spiral where they were discs (the crop in the session's notes, s67-d230). The darkest pixels are the HII
knots inside their clouds (debt #181's points), unchanged by either.

**The checks.** vitest 436 passed (cloudShape.test.ts: the cap's half-maximum, the face-on raster unchanged by the cap,
the shear's shape against the read, A_V x area conserved, round to the bit at 0 and without the field, the ring lookup;
TUNING_DEFAULTS pinned with cloudElongation 1); tsc -b; vite build. picture:update once: the Milky Way's five captures
unchanged byte for byte (its defaults draw no clouds' layer); NGC 4414's four moved - field +0.85 % in display mean,
1.72 % of pixels by >= 3/255; star-first +0.62 %, 1.86 %; thumbnail +0.93 %, 1.41 %; zoom stand +1.48 %, 38.6 % (the
clouds resolve there); then the picture test once more: 15 passed, all nine frames the committed pictures byte for byte.

### D231. S67: the clouds' size law from a read source — Lada & Dame 2020's X_CO-corrected Σ_GMC, 82 M☉ pc⁻² inside the solar circle and 35 outside it, the radius held at 150 pc with the mass kept, the dispersion at each cloud's own surface density (#182 opened) (BUILD_III Phase V8, S67; the lead's ruling on an Opus probe, an Opus builder)

**The owner's choice (2026-10-18).** "Smaller giant clouds (model)", of the options measured for the whole-galaxy
clouds' dark orbs (D230). Every cloud's radius was √(M/πΣ) at one `GMC_SURFACE_DENSITY` = 42 (Heyer et al. 2009's
median), so with Rice et al. 2016's inner truncation at 10⁷ M☉ the inner Galaxy's largest clouds were 150-275 pc.

**The reading** (a blind Opus reader, 2026-10-18; `docs/READING_CLOUD_SIZES.md`). Heyer et al.'s 42 is measured over
R 4.1-8.1 kpc only, at a constant X_CO; Lada & Dame 2020, correcting X_CO for its radial gradient, find 82 ± 10 in the
molecular ring and inside it (their 3-5 kpc mean 84.5) and "a single mass surface density of Σ_GMC = 35" outside it;
their constant-X_CO 13 ± 4 at 9-14 kpc and eq. 1 (Σ = 54.5 − 3.7 R) are uncorrected. The Milky Way's largest clouds have
R ~60-150 pc (Miville-Deschenes et al. 2017's largest ~150 pc, "comparable to the molecular disk's scale height").

**The probe** (phase 1, the size law substituted alone, masses and streams unchanged; the session's notes,
probe_s67/size). Eq. 1 made clouds larger (Σ < 42 beyond 3.4 kpc: max 305 pc); the 13 regime enlarged the outer clouds
(to 176 pc at Rice's outer 1.5 × 10⁶); no Σ ≤ 82 brings a 10⁷ M☉ cloud under 150 pc (that needs Σ ≥ 141) - only a cap
does; the mass function already truncates at Rice's M₀ (10⁷ inside R_SUN, 1.5 × 10⁶ outside).

**The ruling (the lead's).**
1. *Two regimes, a step*: `GMC_SURFACE_DENSITY_INNER` = 82 and `GMC_SURFACE_DENSITY_OUTER` = 35 M☉ pc⁻² (level 0,
   `[verified: Lada & Dame 2020]`; Heyer et al.'s 42 in the inner one's about, superseded by the X_CO(R) correction),
   at the cloud's birth radius against `R_SUN` - the one boundary the mass function's truncation uses (`law_for`);
   R_SUN itself is outside. `GMC_SURFACE_DENSITY` is retired. Not the uncorrected 13, which enlarges the outer clouds.
2. *The cap*: `GMC_RADIUS_MAX` = 150 pc (`[verified: Miville-Deschenes et al. 2017]`), the mass kept, so a capped
   cloud's surface density rises (W43's ≈ 460 at R_eq ~70 pc a disclosed check that the giants are denser).
3. *The dispersion at each cloud's own Σ = M/πR²* (Heyer et al. eq. 10, √(GM/5R)), so Mach follows. The test's Mach
   range 20-35 was the model's own S32 number ("Measured at S32"), not a sourced window: re-pinned (max 39.86).
4. *`ngc_4414` takes the same law at the same R*, consistent with the mass function's absolute R_SUN; disclosed - no
   measured cloud census, PHANGS discs' ~100 (Rosolowsky et al. 2021) near the inner regime. At the same R/R_d the
   inner mass function would meet Σ 35 inside 8.2 kpc (clouds to 440 pc under the probe's 13), a coupled change.
5. *`cloud_extinction_v`*: its about meant "the census's one surface density", which no longer exists; it is computed at
   the inner regime's 82 (`clouds.census_extinction_v`), the regime that holds 83 % of the Milky Way's cloud mass and
   every cloud above 1.5 × 10⁶ M☉: 2.9696 → 5.7977 mag (82/42); the about says an outer uncapped cloud's is 2.47 and a
   capped giant's more. No drawing reads it since D228 (region.ts reads `cloud_dust_extinction_v`; only a comment
   names the scalar); `/api/clouds`' header still carries it.

**Built.** `clouds.surface_density_at` and `clouds.cloud_size_law` (radius and effective Σ), read in
`materialise_clouds`; the three constants in the clouds stage's `reads_constants`; the abouts of `cloud_size`,
`cloud_velocity_dispersion`, `cloud_extinction_v`, the stage's docstring and `/api/clouds`' derived column's; the offset
declaration in `layer/cloud_texture.py` re-read to the model. A test by hand
(`test_the_size_law_by_hand_either_side_of_the_solar_circle_and_at_the_cap`): 10⁵ M☉ at 8.19 kpc 19.702 pc, at 8.20
and 8.21 kpc 30.157 pc, 10⁷ M☉ at 4 kpc held at 150 pc with Σ 141.47 and σ_v 7.573 km/s, the A_V 5.7977.

the cell outlines on) their points draw as bloomed discs over the cell outlines' grid, and the metrics read that -

of picture, differing in hand-drawn irregularity"; NGC 4414 "right at a glance in colour, inclination, flocculence
and mottling", with the dust web and complexes still procedural side by side: the Milky Way is there in kind and
differs by more than irregularity (the arms' number, the colour's level, the grain); NGC 4414 is right in
inclination and in its arms' contrast and texture slope, not yet at a glance in colour, flocculence or dust.

**The frames beside the goals (the lead's reading of the committed frames, 2026-10-19).** **The Milky Way** (the
field mode, the owner's defaults, the clouds off): a barred spiral with visible arms, a warm core and a bluer outer
disc - the same kind of picture as the artist's impression, its arms less distinct and less irregular, no dust lanes
drawn by default, the outer disc grainy. **NGC 4414** (now on RGB, its own defaults, the clouds on): an inclined disc
with sheared dust streaks around the bulge (D229-D231 removed the black orbs) and pale HII knots; against Hubble's
picture the bulge is too bright and compact, the outer disc lacks the dense flocculent arm segments and the blue
star-forming complexes, and the dust web is confined to the inner disc.

**3. A defect found and fixed: the ring draw's inversion (F-2-7; Builder C on the lead's ruling).** The audit's bound
"a cloud is placed at most 976 pc from the radius its ring drew" was exceeded because 712 of 16 577 production clouds
(271 of 6 530 on `ngc_4414`) had a *birth* radius below the ring that drew them, by up to 70.8 pc (the grid step 75 pc):
`invert_cdf`'s step table begins at the last zero-CDF grid point below the ring, so `np.interp` for the smallest u
interpolates from outside it. The binners, the nebular ring ratios and row 37's census then counted those clouds one
ring in, while layer on and off agreed with each other — no on/off test could see it; the drawn ring and the binned
ring disagreed. **Ruled:** a cloud's ring is the ring that drew it wherever a per-ring total or per-radius law is read;
`clouds.ring_birth_radius(u, R, weight, lo, hi)` inverts on the ring's own interval and asserts the result in [lo, hi)
(no silent clip); `api/v6_clouds.py` calls it where it re-derives births; `systems.invert_cdf` itself is unchanged for the
two age draws that rely on its step-to-interval meaning. **The two causes separated** (production grid, layer off; A
neither, B the inversion alone, C both): Milky Way clouds / clusters 16 577 / 12 710 unchanged; row 35 −2.055551 →
−2.055711 → −2.055711; row 37 −0.0979016 → −0.0981709 → −0.0983090; outliers 712 → 0 → 0; cloud size median / mean
12.13 / 17.22 → same → 13.40 / 20.04 pc. `ngc_4414`: 6 530 / 5 029; row 35 −1.905206 → −1.905632 → −1.905632; row 37
−0.039091 → −0.038930 → −0.038970; outliers 271 → 0 → 0; sizes 11.78 / 18.44 → same → 12.76 / 20.30. **The same
defect in the star catalogue's level-0 radius (`systems.py:1083`) and the remnants' radius (`bubbles.py:305`) is

### D235. S72, BUILD_IV Phase W2: the template bundles — every galaxy-scale answer the viewer asks of a template computed once and served from files, byte-identical, under the hash of the model's bytes; the body's `stages` found to record the cache's state and changed to the stage closure; the levels below 4 kpc measured and left to the owner's ruling; #199–#201, 132 open

**The commission.** The owner, 2026-10-26, in chat: "read the briefs and start working on the next sessions, continuing
until the context is getting full enough that its time to start in a new session. you're the fable lead agent
orchestrating the project. spawn subagents as needed to carry out the implementation, and since fable usage is
limited, use opus subagents on work that doesn't benefit much from fable capabilities." `BRIEF.md` after S70 named
S72 = Phase W2 (`BUILD_IV.md` §2b, §4b, §5, §7 rulings 6 and 11) and said to ask before starting W2 unless the owner's
word said to go on; this is that word. Row 71 (W3, the gateway) stays the owner's; branch `worktree-session-70-gateway`
(09147c9) is unmerged and untouched. A Fable lead; an Opus probe, an Opus builder and an Opus reviewer, each in its own
worktree, two at once at most (D190–D192's rationing; the 5-hour window 2 → 20 % across the session, the weekly 41 →
44 %). The gateway's `Galaxygen.AppHost.csproj` carried an uncommitted stray `v` in the owner's working tree from
before the session; left as found, not committed, reported.

**What the plan asked and what the probe found first (Opus, `[measured]` unless tagged).** The plan: an export tool
runs the model once per template and writes every metadata route, every published array, `/api/render` per shipped
set, the censuses and `/api/region` per cell at the levels the ruling allows; the service answers from a bundle when
template, layer, query and content hash match, byte-identical, the gate asserting it on every entry; ruling 6's size
bound set after a probe measures the bundle. The probe wrapped `Service.handle` behind the built viewer on :8031 and
drove the real page through the capture list's cameras, stands and switches (112 requests logged with path, query,
bytes, sha256, stages), then costed every route in fresh processes and sampled the per-cell levels. Seven findings
shaped the build:

1. **The viewer's request shape.** Every input-taking request carries the full input vector — seven controls, five
   seeds, `mergers` as JSON including each event's `about` prose — then `model=azimuthal`, then `template=<name>`;
   `layer` is omitted when on and `layer=off` follows the template when off; the metadata routes carry `model=`;
   `/api/version` is never asked. The whole-disc censuses are sent with an explicit window
   (`r_min=0&r_max=30&phi_min=0&phi_max=6.283185307179586&level=0`), and the binary headers echo the window, so a
   request without one differs in bytes (the defaults echo 0.0375 and 29.9625). Only the 1024-cell tile requests go as
   POST (7.6 KB URLs). The Milky Way never asks `/api/clouds` at galaxy scale (`cloudsExtinction: false`, F-4-1).
2. **Star-first.** `bright?table=1` (633 KB), one tile request naming all 1 024 level-0 cells at
   `l_min=35481.33892335753` (Milky Way) / `25118.86431509577` (NGC 4414), then the remainder render
   `only=remainder&l_min=<the same string>`. The tile snaps `l_min` (three spellings, identical bodies); the remainder
   render does not — it echoes `resolved.l_min` and its light moves in the last digits — and the strings are
   JavaScript's spellings of the table's own doubles (1258.9254117941662 where Python's `10**3.1` is …675).
3. **The body is not a function of the request.** All eight binary handlers wrote `"stages": list(ran)` into the
   header: a cold answer lists what ran, its warm repeat says `[]`. Across fresh processes every body of fourteen routes
   was sha256-identical; cold against warm differed only in that key (15 of 731 bodies in the Milky Way layer-on cost
   run; the clusters route returned three sizes in the walk by what was cached). Nothing else varied: no timestamp,
   no random id, no key order, no refusal (#159 never fired, level 3 at 70.8 L☉ included); NaN in the region and
   remnant columns, so bytes are compared, never `np.array_equal`.
4. **Window against cells.** For `region`, `clouds`, `clusters`, `remnants` and `render`, two windows meeting the same
   cells give identical payload columns; only `region`'s header echoes the window. Tiles compose: a multi-cell
   answer's columns are the one-cell answers concatenated (20 of 20 columns at levels 0 and 2), its header's `arrays`,
   `cells`, `count`, `light`, `tile` differ.
5. **The cost.** Metadata 11 entries, 655 KB. Whole-galaxy entries per (template, layer) with all five sets: Milky Way
   on 105.6 MB / 52 s, off 105.2 / 18; NGC 4414 on 85.0 / 38, off 84.5 / 17 (render 9.4 MB × 5, clusters 4.8 MB × 5,
   arrays 28.8 MB, region sample 2.9, clouds 1.8). Per level-k entry (Milky Way on): a tile 6 KB at the landing's
   threshold, 98 KB at 1 kpc, 30 KB at level 1, 80 KB at level 2, 83 KB at level 3 (70.8 L☉, 0.24 s); one cell's
   region at 10⁶ stars 136–198 KB (0.41 s), clouds 10–12 KB, clusters 11–14 KB, remnants 3.3 KB, **render 126 KB of
   which 125 784 B are header** — the layer's galaxy-wide tables (`census_clustering` 63 KB, `gas_fluctuation` 25 KB,
   `spurs` 11 KB) repeated on every windowed render, 31.6 KB with the layer off (#199). The viewer's region regime
   snaps its windows to a lattice: 53 701 windows and 97 646 (window, level) pairs per galaxy below 4 kpc. The totals
   over the four (template × layer), one threshold per tile, rgb only below galaxy scale `[extrapolated from 12–16
   tiles and 8–16 cells per level]`:

   | part | entries | bytes | compute |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | whole-galaxy entries | 1 656 | 380 MB | 125 s |
   | level 0 whole | 28 672 | 1.32 GB | 1.00 h |
   | level 1 whole | 98 304 | 4.94 GB | 3.76 h |
   | **levels 0–1 whole** | **128 632** | **6.64 GB** | **4.80 h** |
   | level 2 whole, extra | | +22.6 GB | +17.2 h |
   | level 3 whole, extra | | +89.9 GB | +77.9 h |

   The thresholds multiply it: the viewer picks one of 153 grid thresholds per frame, and the remainder render needs
   an entry per (threshold, set).
6. **The hash.** `/api/version` hashed `interface/` and `model/galaxy/api/*.py` (1.0 ms); the model's outputs depend
   on every file under `model/galaxy` (85 files, 5.5 MB: 81 `.py`, `data/parsec_isochrones.npz` 3.24 MB,
   `data/nebular_lines.npz`, `layer/vectors.json`) and on nothing read from outside it; hashing all of them costs
   16–17 ms. `git ls-files --eol` shows every text file `w/lf` under `* text=auto eol=lf`, so a Windows checkout and
   the image hash the same bytes.
7. **The merger prose is in every key and every body** (`inputs`, 1 396 B of header): editing a merger's description
   changes every answer's bytes. True before S72; disclosed.

shipped set (`rgb`, `sho`, `hoo`, `wfc3`, `wfc3n`) at `white=6500&precision=f4` and, per set, the remainder render at
the landing's threshold; `/api/blackbody` per set; `clusters` (per set), `clouds`, `remnants` and `region

string, `filters` re-serialised canonically — so spelling and order never matter; a request the service would refuse

request alone:** the eight handlers' header `stages` becomes the stage closure the answer requires (`Outputs.needs`,

`l_min` as the JavaScript spelling of the table's threshold chosen by the viewer's rule (ported from `brightTiles.ts`);

computes; the owner's ruling on the levels decides whether it is wanted); the manifest records the grid's spec and

**The build (Opus; `model/galaxy/api/bundle.py` new, `service.py`, `http.py`, `__main__.py`, `version.py`,

plus `entries/<key>` (the body, no extension); the manifest (`galaxy-bundle/1`) names `model_hash`, `grid`,
`models`, `built_at` and each entry's route, the query as sent, key, bytes, sha256, media and `ran_at_export`.
`Service(bundles=)` reads every manifest at construction: the hash first (`BundleMismatch` naming both — "a mismatch

**#201 — the 500s (builder A; `service.py` `_events`, `_parse_filters`; `bundle.py` `_filters`, `request()`;
`tests/test_api.py`).** Reproduced first: a merger `"time": 1e999` raised `ValueError` from the JSON writer (the
range check passes `inf`: `0.0 <= inf`); a 100 000-deep `filters=` raised `RecursionError`, and so did a 100 000-deep
`mergers=`; `"time": NaN` was already a 400 with the wrong reason. Each is refused at the parse, by name: a
non-finite event number (`math.isfinite` on time, mass_ratio, gas_fraction), a JSON nested too deeply (`RecursionError`
caught at the `json.loads` of either), an integer of more than 4 300 digits (`json.loads` raises a plain `ValueError`,
not a `JSONDecodeError`) and a 401-digit integer (`float()` raises `OverflowError`, which `stages/spectra.py`'s
`_finite` does not catch — handled in the API; the stage's own catch is noted, not changed). The bundle key's

**4. #197, for the owner (the explanation asked for, as given in chat; no action).** #197 is the star catalogue's and the remnants' ring draws
inverting below their ring's inner edge. S70 found the defect in the clouds and fixed it there: every placed census
draws an object's birth radius by inverting a cumulative table along its ring (`invert_cdf`), and the table's steps
began at the last grid point *outside* the ring, so the first step interpolated from below the ring's inner edge —
4.3 % of the clouds were born one ring too far in. The stars (`systems.py`, `STAR_RADIUS`) and the remnants
(`bubbles.py`, `REMNANT_RADIUS`) call the same inversion: on the production grid, layer off, 955 of 20 003 Milky Way
stars (4.8 %) and 995 of 20 004 on NGC 4414 (5.0 %) are born up to 70 pc below their ring, and 64 of 1 464 and 27 of
594 remnants (4.4 %, 4.5 %), up to 71 pc. The fix is the clouds' fix applied to both — the inversion on the ring's
own interval — and is small in code; what makes it a session of its own is what it moves: every star of the
catalogue redraws, so every frame changes (the sample stars, the bright tiles, the region regime's points), D60's
per-region determinism pins re-pin across the suite with the reason, the bundles re-export, and the goal metrics
are re-read. It is a correctness fix of the model's objects (no physics law changes; the ring's own density is
sampled correctly), so it belongs before the deployment phases if the frames deployed are to be the fixed ones, and
after any ruling that would move the catalogue anyway. The owner's word on when.
